architect.title: Model designer
architect.subtitle: Design a new model and train it from nothing, on approved replies and datasets.

drafts.emptyWrite: Save a design from the designer and it appears here.
drafts.emptyRead: A trainer or an administrator can save designs.

remove.title: Remove {name}?
remove.body: The saved design is removed. Models already trained from it aren't affected.

discard.title: Discard the unsaved changes?
discard.body: The designer holds changes that aren't saved. Continuing replaces them.

design.title: Design
design.fresh: A new design, not saved yet.
design.readOnly: Only a trainer or an administrator can save a design or train it.

dense_decoder.name: Decoder
dense_decoder.about: Writes text one token at a time. This is how chat models work.

moe_decoder.name: Mixture of experts
moe_decoder.about: Holds many specialist blocks and uses only a few for each token. It is large but cheap to run.

encoder_decoder.name: Encoder-decoder
encoder_decoder.about: Reads the whole input first, then writes the answer. T5 works this way.

attention.intro: Attention connects each token to the ones before it. Each head follows its own pattern.

feed_forward.intro: Processes each token on its own after attention. Most of a model's parameters sit here.
feed_forward.introMoe: Each layer holds many experts. A router picks a few of them for each token.

tokenizer.intro: The new model reuses the tokenizer of a published model, so it reads text the same way. Training needs one.

training.title: Training step
training.intro: The length of each example and how many go through each step. They set the memory training needs.

layers.label: Layers
layers.hint: Blocks stacked one after another. More layers make a deeper model.

hidden_size.label: Hidden size
hidden_size.hint: How many numbers describe each token inside the model.

heads.label: Attention heads
heads.hint: The hidden size must divide evenly by this number.

kv_heads.label: Key-value heads
kv_heads.hint: Heads share keys and values to save memory. Leave empty for no sharing.

intermediate_size.label: Feed-forward width
intermediate_size.hint: The width of the feed-forward block in each layer.
intermediate_size.hintMoe: The width of the feed-forward block in one expert.

experts.label: Experts
experts.hint: How many experts each layer holds.

experts_per_token.label: Experts for each token
experts_per_token.hint: How many experts each token uses. No more than the experts.

vocab_size.label: Vocabulary size
vocab_size.hint: How many different tokens the model knows. A number below the tokenizer's is raised to match.

context_length.label: Context length
context_length.hint: The longest text the model can keep in view, counted in tokens.

tie_embeddings.label: Share the vocabulary table with the output
tie_embeddings.hint: The same numbers read tokens in and write them out. This saves parameters.

seq_len.label: Sequence length
seq_len.hint: The length of each training example, in tokens.

batch.label: Batch size
batch.hint: How many examples go through together in each step.

tokenizer.label: Tokenizer
tokenizer.hint: The name of a published model on HuggingFace, such as Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B.

vocabulary.raised: The tokenizer of {tokenizer} has a vocabulary size of {tokens}. The counts below use that size.

error.range: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
error.kvNotDivisible: The attention heads must divide evenly by the key-value heads.

results.title: Size and memory
results.fix: This design can't be built yet. Fix the fields that show a message.

breakdown.allActive: All of them work on every token.
breakdown.embeddings_dominate: The vocabulary table makes up {share} of this model. More layers or a wider model would make it more capable for the same size.

memory.title: Memory to train it here
memory.intro: What training needs on this machine, with each kind of optimizer.
memory.noGpu: No GPU found. Training runs on the CPU, which is very slow.
memory.weights: The finished model takes {size} in half precision.

save.name: Name
save.notesHint: Optional. What the design is for.

train.title: Train from nothing
train.intro: A new project holds the model. The model learns from the approved replies and datasets you choose.
train.name: Name of the new project
train.nameHint: The trained model becomes this project's base model.
train.pick: Choose at least one project or dataset.
train.expectation: Training from nothing needs far more examples than customizing an existing model. A small model trained on few replies will mostly repeat them.
train.needTokenizer: Add a tokenizer and save the design.
train.limitHint: Optional. Leave empty to use every row.
train.limitError: Enter a whole number of 1 or more.
train.nothing: Nothing to learn from yet. Import a dataset or approve replies in Chat.

errors.design_invalid: This field needs a whole number.
errors.design_out_of_range: This number is outside the allowed range.
errors.design_not_divisible: The hidden size must divide evenly by the attention heads.
errors.design_odd_head_dim: Each head needs an even width. Choose a hidden size and a number of heads that give one.
errors.design_too_many_active_experts: A token can't use more experts than the model has.
errors.design_tied_only: An encoder-decoder shares its vocabulary table with the output.
errors.tokenizer_needed: Add a tokenizer to the design and save it before training.
errors.nothing_to_learn: There is nothing to learn from yet. Approve replies in Chat or choose a dataset.
errors.dataset_not_ready: The dataset hasn't finished importing. Wait for it to finish or choose another.

encoder_decoder.explain: A model in two parts. The encoder reads the whole input, then the decoder writes the output from it. T5 is one.

kv_heads.explain: Grouped attention. Several attention heads share one set of keys and values. This saves memory at little cost in quality.

experts.explain: In a mixture of experts, each layer holds several feed-forward blocks. A router picks a few of them for each token.

embeddings.explain: Also called embeddings. It turns each token into a list of numbers the model works with. It has one row for every token the model knows.

router.explain: In a mixture of experts, the small part that picks the experts each token goes through.

norms.explain: Small adjustments that keep the numbers inside the model in a steady range. They hold very few parameters.

lm_head.explain: The final table that turns the model's result into a score for every token. When it is shared with the vocabulary table, it adds no parameters.

tokenizer.explain: Cuts text into tokens and turns each piece into a number. A model must run with the tokenizer it was trained with, so a new model reuses a published one.

optimizer.explain: The part of training that adjusts the parameters after each step. It keeps extra numbers for every parameter, so it needs more memory than the model itself. AdamW is the usual one. 8-bit Adam stores those numbers in less space.

activations.explain: Temporary results the model holds while it works through a batch of text. They grow with the batch size and the sequence length.
